questions.question: Choose the option that is the active form of the given sentence. The visitor was astonished at the standards and varieties of the clothes.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the option that is the active form of the given sentence.

The visitor was astonished at the standards and varieties of the clothes.

options.text: The standards and varieties of the clothes has astonished the visitor.
options.html: The standards and varieties of the clothes has astonished the visitor.

options.text: The standards and varieties of the clothes is astonishing the visitor.
options.html: The standards and varieties of the clothes is astonishing the visitor.

options.text: The standards and varieties of the clothes astonished the visitor.
options.html: The standards and varieties of the clothes astonished the visitor.

options.text: The standards and varieties of the clothes had been astonished the visitor.
options.html: The standards and varieties of the clothes had been astonished the visitor.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The standards and varieties of the clothes astonished the visitor.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change it into Active Voice. 
  • The process of transformation is as follows: 
    • The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
      • Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
      • Subject (objective case) + was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
    • Example:
      • Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)
      • They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)
  • Here, in the given question 'The visitor' is the subject. 
  • And 'the standards and varieties of the cloths' is an object. 
  • The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
  • And 'was astonished at' will be changed into 'astonished'. 
  • The preposition 'at' will be removed. 
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 3. 

Correct Sentence: The standards and varieties of the clothes astonished the visitor.  

Additional Information

  • The verb 'surprise' is followed by 'at' when the action is contrary to the expectations.
  • In all other cases, 'surprised by' will be used.
  • Example:
    • I was surprised at his weird behavior.
    • He was surprised by the arrangements.
  • Both of the given sentences are correct because of the different contexts.

questions.question: Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested below, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice. He wasn’t given the information he needed.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested below, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

He wasn’t given the information  he needed.

options.text: Somebody was not given the information he needed.
options.html: Somebody was not given the  information he needed.

options.text: The information he needed wasn’t given to him.
options.html: The information he needed  wasn’t given to him.

options.text: He needed the information he wasn’t given.
options.html: He needed the information he  wasn’t given.

options.text: They didn’t give him the information he needed.
options.html: They didn’t give him the information he needed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "They didn’t give him the information he needed."

Key Points

  • In the given sentence "He wasn’t given the information he needed.", the sentence is in passive voice.
  • In a passive sentence, the object of an action is promoted to the subject position.
  • In this sentence, "He" is this object-turned-subject, the information is what he was supposed to receive (it is the logical object of "giving"), "the information he needed" is the action that was taken, and the action was "given".
  • The actor who gave the information is not specified.
  • When we convert this into an active sentence, we need to promote an actor to the subject position.
  • As the original sentence doesn't specify who the actor is, we can use a generic pronoun like "They" or "Someone".
  • Hence, "They" is an appropriate, unspecified subject who did the action (from the original sentence) of not giving the necessary information to "him" (the recipient).
  • So, the sentence "They didn’t give him the information he needed." is the correct rephrasing of the original sentence from passive voice ("He wasn’t given the information he needed") to active voice ("They didn’t give him the information he needed").
    • ​Here, the focus is shifted from the receiver of the action in the original sentence to the doer of the action.
  • Other options are still in passive voice or they don't preserve the same meaning as the original sentence, so they are incorrect.

Additional Information

  • Given Sentence (Passive Voice): "He wasn’t given the information he needed."
  • Structure: Subject + auxiliary verb (was) + not + past participle (given) + object (the information he needed).
  • Marked Answer (Active Voice): "They didn’t give him the information he needed."
  • Structure: Subject (They) + auxiliary verb (did) + not + base form of verb (give) + indirect object (him) + direct object (the information he needed).
  • In this active voice sentence, the focus has shifted to the doer of the action ("They") instead of the receiver ("him").
  • The subject ("They") actively performs the action ("did not give") on the object ("the information he needed").

The correct answer is "Why did your brother write such a letter?"

 Key Points

  • The original sentence is in passive voice, and the challenge is to convert it into active voice.
  • The correct active voice maintains the original meaning while correctly identifying the subject (your brother) and the action (write).
  • Using the past simple tense "did write" accurately reflects the action taken by the brother.
  • The structure of the question in active voice clearly attributes the action to the brother, enhancing clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3". 

 Additional Information

  • Options 1) and 2) incorrectly suggest ongoing or completed actions that do not match the past simple context of the original passive sentence.
  • Option 4) lacks the auxiliary verb needed for a properly structured question in English.

questions.question: Choose the correct active voice for the passive voice sentence: "The delicious meals had been prepared by the chefs for the guests."
questions.questionHtml: Choose the correct active voice for the passive voice sentence: "The delicious meals had been prepared by the chefs for the guests."

options.text: The chefs had been preparing the delicious meals for the guests.
options.html: The chefs had been preparing the delicious meals for the guests.

options.html: The chefs had prepared the delicious meals for the guests.

options.text: The chefs prepared the delicious meals for the guests.
options.html: The chefs prepared the delicious meals for the guests.

options.text: The chefs have prepared the delicious meals for the guests.
options.html: The chefs have prepared the delicious meals for the guests.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 2' i.e. 'The chefs had prepared the delicious meals for the guests.'


Key Points

  • The original sentence is in the past perfect passive voice.
  • To convert to active voice, the subject in the passive voice becomes the object, and the agent becomes the subject.
  • While transforming, the tense should be preserved. Thus, 'had been prepared' changes to 'had prepared.'
  • Hence, "The delicious meals had been prepared by the chefs for the guests" becomes "The chefs had prepared the delicious meals for the guests."

Therefore, the correct answer is - "The chefs had prepared the delicious meals for the guests."

 Additional Information

  • Option 1: This sentence is in the past perfect continuous tense, not in the past perfect tense. Option 3: This sentence is in the simple past tense, not in the past perfect tense. Option 4: This sentence is in the present perfect tense, not in the past perfect tense.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. An encouraging speech has been given by the coach to the football players.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence. 
An encouraging speech has been given by the coach to the football players.

options.text: The coach was given a ferocious speech to the football players.
options.html: The coach was given a ferocious speech to the football players.

options.text: The coach had given a ferocious speech to the football players.
options.html: The coach had given a ferocious speech to the football players.

options.text: The coach have given a ferocious speech to the football players.
options.html: The coach have given a ferocious speech to the football players.

options.text: The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players.
options.html: The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players."

Key Points 

  • The given sentence is in passive voice.
  • Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
    • Active: Subject + have / has +3rd form of the verb + Object
    • Passive: Subject(Object of Active) + have / has been + 3rd form of the verb + by + Object(Subject of active)
  • Look at the following examples:
    • Active- He has bought a helicopter. 
    • Passive- A helicopter has been bought by him.
    • Active- He has damaged the car.
    • Passive- The car has been damaged by him.
  • Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
    • Subject(Object of Active)- A ferocious speech
    • 3rd form of the verb-  given
    • Object(Subject of active)- the coach
Hence, the correct answer: The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players.

questions.question: Select the correct active form of the following sentence: The traveller was commanded to leave the country by the officer.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct active form of the following sentence:

The traveller was commanded to leave the country by the officer.

options.html: The officer commanded the traveller to leave the country.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The officer commanded the traveller to leave the country.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in passive voice. It is in Simple Past tense.
  • As per the question we have to change it to active voice.
  • The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
    • Subject (objective case) + was + past participle + by Object (subjective case) (Passive voice) + adjunct
    • Subject + past participle + Object (Active voice) + adjunct
  • Example: 
    • A large house was built by her. (Passive voice)
    • She built a large house. (Active voice)
  • The subject of the given sentence is ‘traveller’.
  • The object of the given subject is ‘officer’.
  • The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
  • was commanded will be changed to commanded.
  • Adjunct is a word or phrase that constitutes an optional element or is considered of secondary importance in a sentence.
  • In the given sentence, to leave the country. is the adjunct. 
  • Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - The officer commanded the traveller to leave the country.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Nothing can be achieved without hard work.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active  voice. 

Nothing can be achieved without hard work.

options.text: One has achieved nothing without hard work.
options.html: One has achieved nothing  without hard work.

options.text: One will achieve nothing without hard work.
options.html: One will achieve nothing  without hard work.

options.text: One could achieve nothing without hard work.
options.html: One could achieve nothing  without hard work.

options.text: One can achieve nothing without hard work.
options.html: One can achieve nothing  without hard work.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "One can achieve nothing  without hard work."

Key Points

  • The transformation from passive voice to active voice involves reordering the sentence so that the subject (the "doer" of the action in the sentence) precedes the verb (the action), and the object (the receiver of the action) follows.
  • "Nothing can be achieved without hard work." This sentence is in passive voice, where the object "Nothing" is in the position of the subject.
  • The rule of converting from passive to active voice is as follows:
    • Identify who is performing the action or the "doer".
    • Here, the doer isn't clearly mentioned, so the general "One" is used.
    • Make the "doer" the subject of the sentence and move it before the verb.
    • Change the verb (here "can be achieved") to match this new formulation.
    • Move what was the subject (now the object - "Nothing") after the verb.
  • Applying these rules, the active voice sentence becomes: "One can achieve nothing without hard work."
    • Here, "One" is the doer, "can achieve" is the action being performed, and "nothing" is the result of the action that is being performed.
    • "Without hard work" remains the same as it modifies the verb/action, specifying the conditions in which it takes place.

Therefore, from the above explanation it is clear that the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. The students are made to stand up for the National anthem by the rules of school policy.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.

The students are made to stand up for the National anthem by the rules of school policy.

options.html: By the rules of school policy, students are made to stand up for the National Anthem.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The school policy makes the students stand up for the National Anthem.'

Key Points  

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the passive voice and 'The students' is the subject and 'the school rules' is the object.
  • When we convert this sentence into an active voice, the subject ' The country ' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the school rules' becomes the subject.
  • The passive format "are + V3 (made)" should be converted into the active format "V1 (make)".
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

Additional Information

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Will + be + being + V3 Football will be being played by him
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
